sentences.text:
3. The petitioner has been charge-sheeted with an offence under Sections 376(2)(n)/323/294 of the I.P.C. on the allegations alleged against him(petitioner) that, on the false promise of marriage, he (petitioner) was keeping sexual relationship continuously with the victim, but, when he(petitioner)
refused to marry her(victim)
, then she(victim) lodged the F.I.R. against the petitioner on dated 13.08.2024 and basing upon such F.I.R., case was registered and the investigation was taken up.

4. During investigation the petitioner was arrested on dated 14.08.2024 and was forwarded to the court after being booked with the offences and accordingly, since then the petitioner is in custody.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted for liberal consideration of bail of the petitioner contending that, the informant is a major girl and she was indulged in sexual relationship with the petitioner continuously and secretly, to which, learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State vehemently opposed contending that, the offences committed by the petitioner against the victim are heinous in nature and also against the society, for which, in this heinous nature of offence,
he(petitioner)should not be allowed to go on bail.

6. When the petitioner is in jail custody since 13.08.2024 and when charge-sheet of the case has already been submitted and when the presence of the petitioner before the police for the purpose of any further investigation may not be required and when the petitioner is a young boy of 24 years and when the presence of the petitioner during trial is not unsecured, then at this juncture, by taking the above factors into account, it is felt proper to allow the petitioner to go on bail with stringent Susanta Hantal vs State Of Odisha .....

1 conditions looking to the future safety and security for the informant, her family members as well as interest of the prosecution.
Hence, the bail application filed by the petitioner is allowed 7.

He (petitioner) is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(rupees fifty thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned S.D.J.M., Jeypore with conditions that :-
(i) He (petitioner) shall not involve with similar nature of crime in future.
(ii) He shall appear before the court personally on each date of adjournment of the case without fail till conclusion of trial.

(iii) He (petitioner) shall not terrorize, coerce, influence or threat to the informant/victim, her parents family members and witnesses either directly or indirectly in any manner whatsoever till conclusion of the trial of the case, but, in case of his failure to comply any of the aforesaid conditions, the learned trial court is authorized to cancel his bail order outrightly without seeking any permission for the same from this Court.
8.
Accordingly, the bail application of the petitioner is disposed of finally.

9. Grant certified copy of this order to the petitioner on proper application.
